Subject: Priority lanes & rotation policy for experimental model pilots

Team —

We have a week-long pilot with Soma Labs starting 2026-10-05 that will run a mix of memory-heavy sweeps and short inference workloads. Product wants a clear policy for how we schedule "experimental" traffic vs "canary" vs regular production on Dedicated pools so we don't regress SLOs for existing customers.

High level asks from product/security:
- Define priority lanes (names, allowed burst hours, preemption policy).
- A rotation/eviction policy for KV cache-heavy models so warmups don't starve canaries.
- A short rollback/auto-fallback plan if latency > 250ms p95 for 2 consecutive 10-min windows.

Can ops and infra weigh in on constraints and whether we can safely grant an autoscale policy exception for 10/05–10/12 (pilot week)? I attached a draft priority matrix and a short playbook (see attachments).

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-priority-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), rotation-playbook.md (markdown)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, k.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lanes & rotation policy for experimental model pilots

Thanks Laura — good to get ahead of this. Quick responses and a proposed matrix below.

Constraints from Product: we want to run 3 experimental variants concurrently for up to 48 hours each and a canary stream of ~50 qps for verification. We need predictable warmup windows so the KV cache can be pre-filled without impacting canaries.

Proposed lanes (short):
- Gold Canary: reserved slices; strict latency SLO; preempt-only-by-exec (no silent preemption). Burst: +20% capacity for 2x 10-min windows/day.
- Silver Experimental: timeboxed, removable preemption; allowed to use warmup-prefill but evicted before Gold canaries. Max concurrent experimental slots: 4 per GPU pool.
- Bronze Background: batch/low-priority sweeps; best-effort.

Rotation/eviction: Older experimental job = first to be evicted. When switching an experimental job into a canary lane it must go through a 15-min warmup on isolated slot, then join canary. If p95 latency for Gold Canary > 220ms for two consecutive 5-min checks, route new requests to fallback model variant.

Open questions for infra/ops:
- Dev: can we implement a soft-reservation token so Product can claim warmup tokens that do not immediately block capacity?
- Ops: what is the operational cost (tokens-hours) of holding 4 experimental slots for a week?

I'll refine the matrix and push a one-page doc to Drive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: k.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lanes & rotation policy for experimental model pilots

Laura / Marissa — ops perspective below. We can support the three-lane model but need to codify the autoscale exception carefully. Operational notes:

- Soft-reservation token: feasible. We'll hand out ephemeral "warmup tokens" that reserve cache slots but are charged at a reduced rate; implementation requires a runtime change and an infra rollout. Est. work: 2 sprints + one small canary on staging.
- Temporary autoscale exception: we can allow a higher target for 10/05–10/12, but only if we: (a) cap total burst to a fixed GPU count per pool, (b) set an automatic revert at 10/13 00:00 UTC, and (c) create an alert that pages infra if avg p95 for Gold Canary > 250ms for 20 minutes.
- Cost estimate: conservatively +18% on pool costs for the week if we reserve 4 experimental slots in every production pool (rough ballpark). I'll send a short cost delta tomorrow.

Attachment: ops-runbook excerpt included in rotation-playbook.md. Also looping in Ben for SLA/priority gating.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: k.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Priority lanes & rotation policy for experimental model pilots

Thanks — a few product/roadmap questions from my side:

1) Timeline: if soft-reservations require 2 sprints, we need a temporary manual workaround for the pilot. Can we pair a manual reservation + an ops-runbook step for warmup?
2) Rollback path: can we automate fallback routing at the gateway layer (route to smaller model family) rather than requiring a manual PAUSE on the pilot?
3) Metrics: please confirm which metrics will gate autoscale revert (p95 only, or p95 + error-rate + GPU load?). I prefer p95 + 5xx-rate > 1% over 15 min for revert.

If we agree on a short manual runbook we can approve the 10/05 exception with the auto-revert flags Dev suggested. I can take the manual-runbook ownership if someone drafts the exact steps.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Folks — thanks for the quick input. Agreed next steps:

- Marissa: finalize the priority matrix and one-pager and drop to Drive by 2026-09-24 EOD (link in metadata).
- Dev: publish cost-delta numbers and create the temporary autoscale exception with the caps and auto-revert set to 2026-10-13 00:00 UTC. Please include escalation page/alerting to infra-oncall.
- Karthik: own the manual warmup runbook; Laura will approve the playbook language for exec sign-off.
- Ben: confirm with Sales that granting this week-long exception (with the stated caps) is acceptable to existing reserved customers; if there are conflicts, escalate to me.

Janelle / Simon — looping you both for transparency. Soma Labs: we'll proceed on the assumption we can provide the experimental slots; final confirmation once we verify no conflicts with the reserved customers.

I'll bundle the final one-pager and runbook and request exec sign-off tomorrow morning.

Best,
Laura
